## Current behavior I created a generic table component, which allows to define columns via templates. My problem is: Change-detection is triggered, even if the component is detached due to content projection (see the discussion at https://stackoverflow.com/questions/48096659/interpolation-executed-even-if-changedetectorref-is-detached/48108250). A simplified version of the problem: - the root-component has a H1-Element with a click-handler (the root-component uses ChangeDetectionStrategy.Default) - below the clickable H1-Element is another component, which renders some rows. A template is specified, which defines how to render a row (and a function-call is used to get the value to render. I know, for this case a function doesn't make sense but it illustrates the problem) - the component, which renders the row, is detached from change-Detection - if I click on the h1-Element, the function is invoked again for each row in the component, although it is detached from change-detection. **Code (from an angular-CLI project):** The code can be found at https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-zcyf9w?file=app%2Fapp.component.ts ### app.component.html ```

Klick me

{{getName(row)}} ``` ### app.component.ts ``` @Component({ selector: 'app-root', templateUrl: './app.component.html' }) export class AppComponent { rows: any[]; constructor(private changeDetectorRef: ChangeDetectorRef, private renderer: Renderer2) { this.rows = this.createRows(100); } getName(row:any): string { console.log("getName called") return row.name; } onClick() { console.log("clicked"); } private createRows(count:number): any[] { let rows: any[] = []; for (let i=0; i < count; i++) { rows.push({ name: "TEST " + (i+1) }) } return rows; } } ``` ### rows.component.html ```
``` ### rows.component.ts ``` @Component({ selector: 'app-rows', templateUrl: './rows.component.html' }) export class RowsComponent { @Input() rows: any[]; @ContentChild(TemplateRef) template: TemplateRef; constructor(private changeDetector: ChangeDetectorRef) { } ngAfterViewInit() { this.changeDetector.detach(); } } ``` I understand, that the change-detection is triggered, because of content-projection. ## Expected behavior There should be a way to prevent check of projected views. The function `markParentViewsForCheckProjectedViews ` in `utils.ts` updates the state of **ALL** views in the hierarchy with `ViewState.CheckProjectedViews`. Proposed solution: - introduce a new ViewState: `ProjectedViewsDetached` - Extend `ChangeDetectorRef `with new methods `detachProjectedViews()` and `reattachProjectedViews()` (which sets/removes the view-state `ProjectedViewsDetached`) - Change the function `markParentViewsForCheckProjectedViews` to something like this: ``` export function markParentViewsForCheckProjectedViews(view: ViewData, endView: ViewData) { let currView: ViewData|null = view; while (currView && currView !== endView) { if (currView.state & ViewState.ProjectedViewsDetached) { currView.state &= ~ViewState.CheckProjectedViews; } else { currView.state |= ViewState.CheckProjectedViews; } currView = currView.viewContainerParent || currView.parent; } } ``` This way I could change the ngAfterViewInit()-lifecycle method of rows.component.ts to ``` ngAfterViewInit() { this.changeDetector.detach(); this.changeDetector.detachProjectedViews(); } ``` This solution should fix this type of problems and does not change the behaviour of applications, which do not use the method `detachProjectedViews()` of the `ChangeDetectorRef`. A simpler solution might be just to change markParentViewsForCheckProjectedViews without introducing a new ViewState: ``` export function markParentViewsForCheckProjectedViews(view: ViewData, endView: ViewData) { let currView: ViewData|null = view; while (currView && currView !== endView) { if (currView.state & ViewState.Attached) { currView.state |= ViewState.CheckProjectedViews; } else { currView.state &= ~ViewState.CheckProjectedViews; } currView = currView.viewContainerParent || currView.parent; } } ``` But this solution might create side-effects on existing applications. ## Minimal reproduction of the problem with instructions See the running example at https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-zcyf9w?file=app%2Fapp.component.ts ## What is the motivation / use case for changing the behavior? I need tables with a lot of rows ( > 1000) to perform well. I'm aware of solutions like virtual scrolling but that introduces other issues (e.g.: dynamic height of table-rows, which makes it nearly impossible to calculate a correct height of the entire table). ## Environment
